NONE: › a strange habit or characteristic that is seen as not important and not harming anyone
（無傷大雅的）怪癖，小毛病，小缺點

example: We all have our little foibles.
我們都有自己的小毛病。

NONE: › the liver of a goose or duck that has been fed to make it fat, eaten as food
› also pâté de foie gras a thick, smooth, soft food made from the liver of a goose or duck that has been fed to make it fat

U: › [ U ] a very thin sheet of metal, especially used to wrap food in to keep it fresh
（尤指用來包裹食品以保鮮的）箔

C: › [ C ] something or someone that makes another's good or bad qualities more noticeable
› [ C ] a thin, light sword used in the sport of fencing

NONE: › to prevent someone or something from being successful

example: The older, cynical character in the play is the perfect foil for the innocent William.
劇中年邁、憤世嫉俗的人物角色正好襯托出威廉的天真單純。
The prisoners' attempt to escape was foiled at the last minute when police received a tip-off.
由於警方收到密報，囚犯的越獄企圖在最後一刻被挫敗。

NONE: › to force someone to have or experience something they do not want

example: I try not to foist my values on the children but it's hard.
我儘量不把我的價值觀強加到孩子們頭上，但是這並不容易。
